findings.title: Mismatched Asset Resolutions
findings.where: Arena, Road, and City screens (background textures)
findings.problem: The ground textures are heavily pixelated and blurry, while the central car sprite and UI elements are rendered at a much higher, crisp resolution.
findings.why: It shatters visual cohesion. The background looks like a zoomed-in, low-resolution placeholder or a texture-streaming bug, making the game look broken rather than intentionally retro.
findings.fix: Replace the ground textures with assets that match the native texel density of the car sprite, or apply a pixelation shader to the car to unify the visual style.

findings.title: Dead Radar Instrument
findings.problem: The radar background is a near-black, featureless disc with very faint concentric rings and no sweep line, crosshair, or prominent grid.
findings.why: It fails to read as a functional, active instrument. At a glance, the lack of contrast and animation makes it look like an empty void or a broken UI element rather than a spatial awareness tool.
findings.fix: Brighten the concentric grid lines, add an intersecting crosshair for the center axis, and include a semi-transparent sweeping radial gradient to simulate an active scan.

findings.title: Broken Scale Hierarchy
findings.problem: The player's car sprite is visually larger than the surrounding industrial buildings and warehouses.
findings.why: It destroys the fantasy and spatial logic of navigating an open-world city. When the vehicle is larger than a factory, the player feels like they are driving on a miniature board game map rather than exploring a dangerous wasteland.
findings.fix: Drastically scale down the car sprite while in the city view to roughly 15% of its current size so it fits realistically alongside or inside the building assets.

findings.title: Flat Typographic Hierarchy
findings.problem: Every piece of text—labels, stat values, headers, and instructions—uses the exact same monospace font size and weight, relying only on layout and thin borders for structure.
findings.why: The player's eye has no clear path to follow. Important actionable elements like the 'CONFIRM' button blend in completely with static, repetitive lists like 'Weapon 1 (empty)', slowing down the vehicle building process.
findings.fix: Increase the font size and weight of major category headers ('COST', 'LEGALITY') and the 'CONFIRM' button. Drop the opacity of all non-actionable '(empty)' text to 40%.

findings.title: Low Contrast Warning Text
findings.where: Arena and Road screens (top-right HUD, 'Plant & Driver' panel)
findings.problem: The status text 'Body armor: x 0/3' is rendered in a dark, saturated red against a dark gray background.
findings.why: It fails baseline contrast standards, making it nearly invisible in peripheral vision. In a high-speed combat game, critical negative status indicators must be instantly readable at a glance.
findings.fix: Change the warning text to a brighter, more luminous color—like safety orange or a bright pastel red—or keep it white and place a bright red warning icon next to it.
